title: Transactional Writing: Applications, Reports and Speeches
summary: Format, register and content for letters of application and CVs, formal reports, speeches, reviews and newspaper articles, at 180–200 words.

notes.text: Grade 11 HL transactional texts are usually **180–200 words** (body only). Marks are given for content, planning and format, and for language, style and editing.

items: **Letter**: formal layout; refer to the advertisement (where and when it appeared); state the position; highlight relevant skills and experience; say why you are suitable; mention the attached CV; request an interview.
**CV**: personal details, education, skills, work experience, achievements, interests, references. Keep it clear and in point form.

rows: Who asked for the report and why
How information was gathered (survey, interviews, observation)

notes.text: Address the audience ('Principal, staff and fellow learners…'); open with a hook; organise points clearly; use **rhetorical devices** (rhetorical questions, repetition, the rule of three, inclusive pronouns); end memorably and thank the audience.

items: **Review** (film, book, restaurant, music): title of the work, brief overview without spoilers, strengths and weaknesses, a rating or recommendation.
**Newspaper article**: headline, byline, lead paragraph answering who, what, when, where, why; quotations from witnesses; the most important information first (inverted pyramid).

questions.prompt: What is the usual length of a Grade 11 HL transactional text?
Which section of a report explains how information was gathered?
What is the line giving the writer's name in a newspaper article called?
A good review should reveal the ending of a film.
A CV should be clear and may be written in point form.
Match each report section to its content.

questions.prompt: Write a lead paragraph for a school newspaper article about a learner who won a national science competition.
questions.memo:
✓ Who and what (1)
✓ When and where (1)
✓ Concise, formal, factual style (1)

questions.prompt: Name THREE things the body of a letter of application should include.
questions.memo: Any three: ✓ reference to the advertisement ✓ the position applied for ✓ relevant skills/experience ✓ why you are suitable ✓ mention of the attached CV ✓ request for an interview (3)

questions.prompt: Write an engaging opening for a speech on bullying to your school assembly.
questions.memo:
✓ Correct address of the audience (1)
✓ An effective hook, e.g. a question, statistic or anecdote (1)

questions.prompt: Explain the 'inverted pyramid' structure of a news article.
questions.memo:
✓ The most important information comes first (1)
✓ followed by less important details, so readers get the key facts quickly (1)
